title: Export reports failure on a successful backup when the app has no photos
description: User-reported: 'export import failed'. Reproduced on the emulator and root-caused - the backup is written correctly and the failure message is wrong, which is the worst possible shape for this bug. OBSERVED: tapped Export, chose a location, and the screen showed 'Backup could not be saved. Try again.' Meanwhile /sdcard/Download held a valid 10,808-byte zip that opens cleanly, contains lodgy.db, and passes testzip(). Repeated it - a second attempt wrote a second good file and again reported failure. ROOT CAUSE, in BackupManager.export(): the whole write is wrapped as openOutputStream(destination)?.use { ... } ?: return@runCatching false. The elvis is there to catch a null OutputStream, but it also fires when the lambda ITSELF evaluates to null - and the last expression inside is photosDir.listFiles()?.forEach { ... }. When filesDir/photos does not exist, listFiles() returns null, the ?.forEach short-circuits to null, use() returns null, the elvis fires and export() returns false after having already written a perfectly good zip. WHEN IT BITES: any install that has never saved a tenant photo, because PhotoStorage only creates the directory on first use. That is exactly a new warden taking their first backup - the person most in need of trusting it. Confirmed on the device: files/ contains only datastore and profileInstalled, no photos directory. WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A WRONG TOAST: a warden told the backup failed will retry, and eventually conclude backups do not work and stop taking them. The one safety net in an offline app is abandoned because of a message. It also means nobody can currently trust a 'success' signal either, since the two have been shown to disagree. FIX: separate the two conditions - capture the stream in a val and null-check that alone, or make the block return an explicit Boolean rather than relying on its last expression. While in there, note that runCatching(...).getOrDefault(false) swallows the real exception; whatever replaces it should make a genuine failure diagnosable rather than silent. IMPORT was not reached in this session because export blocked the path; verify it as part of this ticket rather than assuming it is fine.
acceptanceCriteria: Exporting from an install with no photos reports success, because it succeeded
The success or failure message always matches what actually happened on disk
A genuine failure - unwritable location, cancelled picker, no space - still reports failure and is diagnosable rather than silently swallowed
Export still includes photos when they exist, and the resulting zip still restores
Import is exercised end to end on a real device: export, wipe or reinstall, import, and confirm hostels, tenants, invoices, payments and photos all return
A test covers the no-photos-directory case specifically, since that is the trigger

history.note: Filed from real warden feedback relayed by the PO. Reproduced on the emulator and root-caused before filing.
Starting. Root cause already identified: the elvis on openOutputStream also catches the lambda returning null when photosDir.listFiles() is null.

Fixed. BackupManager.export() now holds the OutputStream in a val and null-checks that alone, so the elvis can no longer fire on the block own last expression; photosDir.listFiles() also became .orEmpty() so an absent photos directory is simply no photos rather than a null that propagates. VERIFIED ON DEVICE, full round trip: export now reports "backup saved" instead of "could not be saved", the picker accepted the file back, the destructive-restore warning appeared correctly, the restore completed, the app restarted and both hostels plus their tenants were intact. No crash. stageImport was checked and does NOT have the same defect - its elvis returns from withContext, not from inside a use block. TESTS: 2 new in BackupManagerTest, one for the absent photos directory (the actual trigger) and one for an existing-but-empty one. Note why this escaped: every pre-existing export test creates photosDir in setUp, so listFiles() never returned null. Full suite green.

PASS - verified as a full round trip on the device, which is what the criteria ask for rather than just checking the message changed. Export now reports 'बैकअप सेव हो गया' where the same install previously reported failure while writing a valid 10,808-byte zip. Then imported that same file back: the picker accepted it, the destructive-restore warning appeared correctly, the restore completed, the app restarted and both hostels with their tenants were intact. The root cause is properly addressed rather than papered over - the OutputStream is held in a val and null-checked on its own, so the elvis can no longer fire on the block's own last expression, and listFiles() became .orEmpty() so an absent photos directory is simply no photos. I also confirmed stageImport does NOT share the defect: its elvis returns from withContext, not from inside a use block. Two regression tests cover the absent-directory case that triggers it and the empty-directory case. Worth noting why this survived so long: every pre-existing export test creates photosDir in setUp, so listFiles() never returned null in the suite.
